Setup: 7 lands (4 Island, 3 Swamp). Key interaction: Winding Constrictor makes each Archfiend of Ifnir trigger put **two** -1/-1 counters on every opposing creature (including Constrictor itself), so a few discards wipe the opponent's board, while Shadowstorm Vizier grows with every discard.

1. Cast Brilliant Spectrum paying {U}{B} + 2 more (Island, Island, Swamp, Swamp) — converge X = 2. Draw two cards (both Swamps). Discard Elder Deep-Fiend and one Swamp.
   - Two discard events: Vizier becomes 3/5. Archfiend triggers twice → each opposing creature gets 2 -1/-1 counters per trigger (Constrictor's replacement). After both: Rishkar (4/4) and Tireless Tracker (5/4) are 0/0 and die; Constrictor is 3/4; Gearhulk is 5/5.
2. Play the other Swamp as your land for the turn (remaining untapped: 2 Islands, 2 Swamps).
3. Cycle Horror of the Broken Lands ({B}). Draw a Swamp. Vizier → 4/6. Archfiend trigger: Constrictor → 1/2, Gearhulk → 3/3.
4. Cycle Floodwaters ({2}, Island + Island). Draw a Swamp. Vizier → 5/7. Archfiend trigger: Constrictor → -1/0 and dies; Gearhulk → 1/1.
5. Activate Stromkirk Condemned: discard a Swamp. Vampires (Stromkirk) get +1/+1 → 3/3. Vizier → 6/8. Archfiend trigger: Constrictor is gone, so Gearhulk gets just one -1/-1 counter → 0/0 and dies. The opponent now controls no creatures.
6. Attack with Archfiend of Ifnir (5/4 flying), Shadowstorm Vizier (6/8 flying), and Stromkirk Condemned (3/3). There are no possible blockers: 5 + 6 + 3 = 14 damage, exactly lethal against 14 life.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

content.thinking:
I'm counting up our mana resources - 4 Islands and 3 Swamps for 7 total mana, with no land in hand but noting that Brilliant Spectrum could dig into the deck and find a Swamp to play for an 8th land drop.

Opponent's board is at 14 life with Winding Constrictor as a 7/8, Verdurous Gearhulk at 9/9 trample, Rishkar 4/4, and Tireless Tracker 5/4, all pumped with +1/+1 counters. On our side we have Shadowstorm Vizier, Archfiend of Ifnir, and Stromkirk Condemned. The key interaction: Archfiend triggers a -1/-1 counter on all opponent creatures per discard, but Winding Constrictor doubles counter placement, so each discard actually deals -2/-2 to everything they control, including Constrictor itself. Working through the math, two discards kill Rishkar and Tracker, while four discards would be enough to kill Constrictor too and leave Gearhulk at just 1 toughness.

I'm figuring out that a fifth discard, once Constrictor is dead, finishes off Gearhulk with a plain -1/-1, wiping their whole board with five total discards. Meanwhile, our own creatures benefit from discards too — Vizier grows with each one, and Stromkirk Condemned gets a Vampire lord-style pump — so I need to weigh whether racing to 14 damage is faster than clearing their board first.

Elder Deep-Fiend also comes to mind since its flash and emerge ability could tap down blockers during combat, though it'd still be summoning sick itself; the cheapest emerge costs come from sacrificing the higher-mana-value creatures like Horror or Archfiend. Since none of their creatures fly or have reach, any evasive attackers we have are essentially unblockable right now.

Doing the math: with Vizier and Stromkirk growing off discards, five total discards clears their board and pumps both creatures enough that Archfiend (5) + Vizier (6) + Stromkirk (3) adds up to exactly 14 flying/unblocked damage — a clean lethal line.

I'm also considering an alternate route: Elder Deep-Fiend taps all four of their creatures, clearing blockers that way instead of through discards, though emerging it costs extra mana I'd need to account for. Then I start tallying what discard outlets I actually have available — Stromkirk Condemned's free discard, plus cycling on Horror and Archfiend — to see how many discards I can realistically fit in.

Brilliant Spectrum could also draw and discard two cards via converge, and since Archfiend triggers separately per discarded card, that's two more triggers rather than one. Counting up my total mana (7, possibly 8 if I play a drawn Swamp), I start sketching out a full sequencing plan for the turn.

I need to work out the exact mana allocation for casting Spectrum, paying with a mix of Islands and Swamps so I still have enough U and B left over afterward, then land the new Swamp to get to 4 remaining mana for the next spell.

Now I'm tracing through the discard/cycling sequence: Cycle Horror discards 3, triggers Archfiend and Vizier, shrinking Constrictor and Gearhulk while drawing a Swamp; then Cycle Floodwaters discards 4, killing Constrictor and shrinking Gearhulk further; finally Stromkirk's discard ability pushes the total to 5 discards, which through Archfiend kills Gearhulk outright and pumps Vizier up to 6/8 while Stromkirk sits at 3/3.

With one mana left, attacking with Archfiend (5), Vizier (6), and Stromkirk (3) totals exactly 14 damage against an opponent at 14 life with no blockers left — that's lethal. I'm double-checking the discard math though: after drawing two Swamps, the hand should be Horror, Elder Deep-Fiend, Floodwaters, and two Swamps, so the Spectrum discard should hit Elder Deep-Fiend and one Swamp, then play the remaining Swamp and proceed with the cycling as planned. I want to verify whether keeping Elder Deep-Fiend and discarding differently could reduce the number of discards needed, and I'm re-reading Woodland Wanderer/Constrictor's counter-replacement wording to make sure I'm applying the -1/-1 counter interaction correctly.

Constrictor doubles each -1/-1 counter it would receive, so Archfiend's trigger gives every creature two counters instead of one, including Constrictor itself. Tracking Constrictor's death timing against the Gearhulk's counters: after the fourth discard trigger Constrictor dies, meaning the fifth discard only adds a single counter, and working through the math the Gearhulk ends up at 8 minus counters annihilating down to 1/1 after four triggers, then the fifth pushes it to 0/0 and it dies — the order of Constrictor's death doesn't change the outcome, and 14 damage is still exactly enough regardless. I'm also checking Vizier's cycling trigger wording to confirm it still applies correctly here.

Checking that the opponent has no responses since they're out of cards and no relevant mana abilities matter, then verifying mana totals: 8 lands available covers Spectrum's cost plus both cycling costs with enough black mana from the Swamps to cover Spectrum and Horror's requirements. I'm also considering whether Deep-Fiend is even necessary or if casting Spectrum with a smaller X could work as a simpler line.

Vizier grows with each discard, Archfiend's flying makes blockers irrelevant, and Stromkirk needs the board wiped by the fifth discard trigger — everything checks out, so I'll write up the solution now.
